Real Talk: Nintendo and Capcom - Censorship & How to Fix It

Frankly, I think the whole kerfuffle over Street Fighter V is pretty nonsensical- these are just camera angles. Camera angles. The gameplay's not hurt in the least, nothing is really being lost- that said, making the original angles optional seems like a nice idea, especially considering the fallout over it.

Regarding Xenoblade Chronicles X, I certainly think that something was lost, and that it sends the wrong sorts of messages about what constitutes normalcy- I'm glad that was brought out in this video.

Why is this even seen as an issue worth discussing. The whole thing is blown out of proportion, and the games are not really hurt by these design choices. Calling this censorship does a disservice to the word.

Maybe the Street Fighter example isn't actually a serious issue, just something done the wrong way (on the sly), but both are, without a shadow of doubt, examples of censorship because censorship is simply the act of the removing objectionable or sensitive content.

"done the wrong way", wtf? They're not obligated to report to anyone. It's kinda their game. I think they understand that most rational people won't give a shit.

People are blowing up over this as though they have some right to dictate the contents of the game. If the lack of a few upskirts bothers people that much, don't buy the game and move on. Don't sit here and try to make it sound like they're suddenly the North Korea of the gaming industry.

I'm sorry, but a company who's business is making a product is obligated to answer to their consumers. In the case of Street Fighter, it could be as simple as "this was our intent from the start" or "we did this to maintain a T rating" or some other acknowledgement of the change. I don't have an issue with the change; I don't play Street Fighter, and wouldn't have known this was a thing if people had been making videos about it.

The Xenoblade issue is something else entirely since it's a result of localization (and therefore only in the North American release) and is an omission of a customization feature that some people may like to have to have a more representative avatar in-game.

I don't like the hyperbole of connecting censorship to North Korea. If I want to say the idea is "fucking retarded", but choose to use different words to suit the discourse or forum, that's still an act of censorship. I am censoring my own words out of consideration to the inappropriateness of them. That doesn't mean that suddenly I'm a dictator ruthlessly oppressing my own thoughts. Censorship simply is any alteration done on the basis of something being (or being considered) objectionable or inappropriate. Yes, there are places where this is done to silence dissent and oppress the populace, but that doesn't mean censorship is inherently authoritarian.

No, they are not obligated to answer to you about their design decisions, just like you are not obligated to buy the game. When such a company does engage with consumers to accept their input, it's usually because it's to the companies' advantage to do so. There is no advantage to taking a few vocal idiots seriously. Most people won't care about this change.
